theory.intro: A **quadratic** $y=ax^{2}+c$ and an **exponential** $y=a^{x}$ are both non-linear, so their graphs are not straight lines. Graph either one like a line: build a table of values, plot the columns as points, then join them with a smooth curve.
facts: A **quadratic** $y=ax^{2}+c$ has $x^{2}$ as its highest power.
Its graph is a smooth U-shape called a **parabola**, opening upward when $a>0$ and downward when $a<0$.
An **exponential** $y=a^{x}$ has the variable $x$ in the **power**.
Its graph is a smooth curve that grows or decays one way and never reaches the $x$-axis.
For $y=a^{x}$, consecutive $y$-values change by a **common ratio** equal to the base $a$.
So for $y=2^{x}$ the $y$-values double each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Negative $x$-values are allowed, and for $y=2^{x}$ they give fractions: $2^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}$, $2^{-2}=\frac{1}{4}$.
steps: Substitute each value of $x$ into the equation to complete the table
Plot each column of the table as a coordinate point
Join the points with a smooth curve

foundation.question_text:
Copy and complete the table of values for $y=x^{2}$, then plot the graph.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccccc} x & -3 & -2 & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ y &  &  &  &  &  &  &  \end{array}$
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=6.8cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3.6,xmax=3.6,ymin=-1.5,ymax=10.5,xtick={-3,-2,-1,1,2,3},ytick={2,4,6,8,10},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[draw=none,mark=none] coordinates {(0,0)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Substitute each value of $x$ into the equation to complete the table.**
$\begin{array}{c|ccccccc} x & -3 & -2 & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ y & 9 & 4 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 9 \end{array}$

Each column gives one point, for example $(1,\;1)$.
3. **Join the points with a smooth curve.**

mastery.question_text: Construct a table of values for both $y=x^{2}$ and $y=2^{x}$ using $x=0,1,2,3,4$, then plot both curves on the same axes.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Substitute each value of $x$ into the equation to complete the table.**
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ x^{2} & 0 & 1 & 4 & 9 & 16 \\ 2^{x} & 1 & 2 & 4 & 8 & 16 \end{array}$
2. **Plot each column of the table as a coordinate point.**
The two curves meet where the columns match, at $(2,\;4)$ and $(4,\;16)$.
3. **Join the points with a smooth curve.**
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=6.8cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-0.3,xmax=4.6,ymin=-1.5,ymax=17.5,xtick={1,2,3,4},ytick={4,8,12,16},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=0:4,samples=80]{x*x};\addplot[thick,red,<->,domain=0:4.05,samples=60]{exp(x*ln(2))};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.5pt,black] coordinates {(0,0) (1,1) (2,4) (3,9) (4,16)};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.5pt,red] coordinates {(0,1) (1,2) (2,4) (3,8) (4,16)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

mastery.question_text: An exponential curve $y=a^{x}$ passes through the points where $x=1,\;y=5$ and $x=2,\;y=25$. Find the base $a$, then construct a table of values for $x=-1,0,1,2$ and plot the curve.
mastery.solution_text:
The $y$-values are multiplied by the common ratio $a$ each step, and $25\div 5=5$, so $a=5$ and $y=5^{x}$.
1. **Substitute each value of $x$ into the equation to complete the table.**
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ y & \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 5 & 25 \end{array}$
2. **Plot each column of the table as a coordinate point.**
Each column gives one point, for example $x=1$ gives $(1,\;5)$.
3. **Join the points with a smooth curve.**
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=6.8cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1.4,xmax=2.4,ymin=-2,ymax=27,xtick={-1,1,2},ytick={5,10,15,20,25},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,red,<->,domain=-1.35:2.05,samples=60]{exp(x*ln(5))};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.5pt,black] coordinates {(-1,0.2) (0,1) (1,5) (2,25)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
